description: OAuth callback state query param reaches res.redirect on the error path, where the getSafeRedirectUrl guard applied on the success path at L120 is omitted, so an off-site target is redirected to.
demotionReason: Mitigation is BROKEN/BYPASSABLE, so the truth table's broken row applies; with medium severity that row yields an advisory rather than a gate-block, and this is not a soundness demotion. getSafeRedirectUrl covers only the success path at packages/app-store/larkcalendar/api/callback.ts:120, while the catch path at :125 passes state.returnTo straight into res.redirect. returnTo is UNAUTHENTICATED: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:15-17 computes, and packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:26-32 verifies, an HMAC over the string `${state.nonce}:${userId}` only, so returnTo sits outside the MAC, is taken verbatim from the state supplied on the callback, and any state already issued for that user can be replayed with returnTo swapped for an attacker-chosen target. Impact stays medium because the redirect target receives no authorization code, token or other credential, making this a phishing pivot rather than a credential leak.

description: POST /v2/oauth/:clientId/authorize appends the new authorization code to the caller's own redirectUri after only the wildcard origin matcher screened it, so an attacker host can receive that code.
demotionReason: No demotion; this is the truth table's broken-mitigation row on a critical sink. Bypass: redirectUri arrives as a bare @IsString() with no scheme or host constraint at apps/api/v2/src/modules/oauth-clients/inputs/authorize.input.ts:4-5, and the only screen is isOriginAllowed at apps/api/v2/src/modules/oauth-clients/controllers/oauth-flow/oauth-flow.controller.ts:63, whose helper escapes the stored pattern then rewrites the escaped asterisk to dot-star at apps/api/v2/src/lib/is-origin-allowed/is-origin-allowed.ts:11-12; dot-star also spans / ? and #, so the pattern https://*.example.com compiles to ^https://.*\.example\.com$ and https://evil.com/x?y=.example.com satisfies it, after which :80 sends the code to evil.com. Verified by executing that exact helper in-tree, not by inspection. Precondition is one stored redirectUris entry containing an asterisk, chosen by the client owner and not by the caller; exact-string entries take the strict-equality branch at is-origin-allowed.ts:6 and are safe. Reachable in production without admin rights: the route sits behind NextAuthGuard at oauth-flow.controller.ts:50, so the victim's own session suffices. mitigation-inventory.txt lists only the two @UseGuards lines for this file at :50 and :110, so the redirectUri screen itself falls outside the mitigation column's nine patterns - a recall limit, not an absence of code. Corroborates Layer 1 findings at the same line and at is-origin-allowed.ts:12.

description: subscriberUrl accepted by POST /api/webhooks with its URL check commented out is fetched server-side here with no private-range filter, deny-list or DNS-rebinding check, reaching internal hosts.
demotionReason: No demotion; recorded to explain the exposure. Mitigation is None on four write paths and DNS-blind on the other two. NO SSRF CHECK AT ALL: apps/api/v1/pages/api/webhooks/_post.ts:75 and apps/api/v1/pages/api/webhooks/[id]/_patch.ts:78 parse with schemas whose subscriberUrl constraint is commented out at apps/api/v1/lib/validations/webhook.ts:18, so both the v1 create and the v1 update path store an internal target behind a plain non-admin API key; packages/app-store/zapier/api/subscriptions/addSubscription.ts:16 and packages/app-store/make/api/subscriptions/addSubscription.ts:26 read subscriberUrl straight from req.body with only API-key authentication and no URL validation. DNS-BLIND SYNCHRONOUS VALIDATION, which is a different failure from having no mitigation: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/webhook/create.handler.ts:28 and apps/api/v2/src/modules/webhooks/utils/validate-webhook-url.ts:5 do call the validator, but it self-documents no DNS-rebinding protection at packages/lib/ssrfProtection.ts:193-196, so it cannot see a host that answers public at save time and private at delivery time, and the async variant swallows lookup failures at packages/lib/ssrfProtection.ts:185-187. All four rule-1 criteria hold.

description: The scheduled-trigger cron fetches each stored subscriberUrl with no re-validation and no timeout, so a URL registered through an unvalidated writer is fetched server-side on the next cron tick.
demotionReason: No demotion; None-mitigation row on a high-severity sink. Criterion (4) holds even though the cron route is CRON_API_KEY gated: the attacker's only action is registering the URL through one of the unvalidated writers, after which the cron fires on schedule with no further attacker input, so no privileged access is needed to reach the fetch. No re-validation and no timeout or AbortSignal are applied. J10 defects on this path, recorded here as the per-path gate rationale and deliberately NOT copied from the other dispatcher: the signature header is added only inside if (webhook) at L63 while the lookup swallows its own error at L52, so a transient database fault sends the payload UNSIGNED rather than failing; the fetch at this line is never awaited and its .catch only console-logs, so a non-2xx or network failure is discarded; the scheduled row is deleted at L79 before that fetch resolves, so a failed delivery is unrecoverable; and the closing Promise.allSettled at L86 is NOT awaited, so the handler can return before deliveries settle. Those lines match no Layer 3a sink pattern and are reported in Layer 1 category 4. CREDITED MITIGATION: redirect: "manual" at L72.

description: The tasker dispatcher fetches the stored subscriberUrl with no re-validation, timeout or abort signal, so a URL registered via an unvalidated writer reaches internal hosts on the default send path.
demotionReason: No demotion; None-mitigation row on a high-severity sink. Source is the same stored subscriberUrl enumerated on the sendPayload finding - four writers apply no SSRF check at all. This is the DEFAULT path, not an opt-in one: sendWebhookDirectly is the else branch taken whenever TASKER_ENABLE_WEBHOOKS is not "1". No re-validation runs before the fetch and no timeout or AbortSignal is set, so a slow sink also holds the worker open. J10 defects on this path, recorded here as the per-path gate rationale: the payload template only selects a Content-Type while the body at L88 is always the JSON envelope, so a non-JSON template makes the request declare form-urlencoded and is otherwise ignored (L86); a subscriber row with no secret yields an empty signature and the X-Cal-Signature-256 header is omitted at L103, so delivery is unsigned and fail-open (L94); the subscriber's own responseText from L114 is returned as message at L119 and logged unbounded at L167; and the outer catch at L33 converts a delivery throw into ok:false, so the inner re-throw at L182 never runs, the awaited allSettled at L186 records "fulfilled" and the success tally at L190 counts failures as sent. Those four lines match no Layer 3a sink pattern and are reported in Layer 1 category 4 per check 16. CREDITED MITIGATION: redirect: "manual" at L111 denies the redirect pivot, which narrows the SSRF but does not remove it.

description: The unvalidated Content-Type header read at L31 is interpolated into a console-only tslog record, so a caller can pollute log fields; the sink is stdout, with no remote or Sentry transport.
demotionReason: Mitigation is functionally sound but incomplete, so the functional-but-limited row applies. The sink is corrected here: apps/web/app/api/parseRequestData.ts:4 imports @calcom/lib/logger, which is tslog configured with a CONSOLE transport only, so the earlier claim that this value reaches a remote log platform and Sentry was unsupported and is withdrawn - stdout capture by a hosting platform is deployment-dependent and is not a code-proven sink. Node's HTTP header parser rejects raw CR and LF in a header value, so log-entry splitting is unreachable and only field pollution remains; mitigation-inventory.txt lists no sanitising wrapper for this file; and the handler aborts with HttpError 415 at apps/web/app/api/parseRequestData.ts:50 immediately after logging, so the tainted value never reaches an authorization or persistence path. Severity is lowered from medium to low because the removed clauses were carrying it.

description: The global exception filter logs the full request body and Authorization header for every rejected request, so a token call refused by the validation pipe still records the client secret it carried.
demotionReason: No demotion; None-mitigation row, and high rather than critical only because the successful-path legs already cover the issued tokens. This is the leg that defeats the obvious workaround: even a request that never reaches a controller is logged in full. Source: the same POST /v2/auth/oauth2/token at apps/api/v2/src/modules/auth/oauth2/controllers/oauth2.controller.ts:65, reached here whenever that call is rejected. The line logs the exception object together with body: request.body at L23, headers: filterReqHeaders(request.headers) at L24 and ...userContext at L28. It compounds with the validation pipe, which is configured with validationError target: true and value: true at apps/api/v2/src/bootstrap.ts:76-77, so the rejected payload is embedded in the exception as well as logged beside it. Registered by app.useGlobalFilters in bootstrap.ts, so it is unavoidable for any HttpException. Mitigation is None for the same reason as the other legs: filterReqHeaders re-emits Authorization verbatim. Same Winston egress via main.ts:113.

description: Every response body is JSON-stringified into a global log record with the caller's email, so the OAuth token endpoint writes the access and refresh tokens it just issued into the log stream.
demotionReason: No demotion; None-mitigation row on a critical sink. This is the response leg of the same chain and is reported separately because the data it exposes is different: the tokens the server MINTED, not the secrets the client sent. Source: the same POST /v2/auth/oauth2/token at apps/api/v2/src/modules/auth/oauth2/controllers/oauth2.controller.ts:65, whose success response carries access_token and refresh_token. Sink: this line logs responseBody = JSON.stringify(data) built at L30 together with ...userContext at L44, and apps/api/v2/src/lib/extract-user-context.ts:21 sets userEmail = user.email, so subscriber PII is logged alongside the credential. Registered globally as APP_INTERCEPTOR in app.module.ts, so it applies to every route including /v2/auth/oauth2/token. No redaction exists between the handler's return value and the logger call, and mitigation-inventory.txt lists no sanitiser for this file. Egress is the same Winston pipeline wired at apps/api/v2/src/main.ts:113 - console unconditionally, Axiom when both AXIOM_TOKEN and AXIOM_DATASET are set. An issued refresh token is a bearer credential with a long life, which is why this is critical rather than high.

description: Every request body is JSON-stringified into a global log record together with the Authorization header, so POST /v2/auth/oauth2/token writes client secrets, auth codes and PKCE verifiers to the log.
demotionReason: No demotion; the truth table's None-mitigation row on a critical sink, so all four rule-1 criteria hold. Source: any client's request to apps/api/v2/src/modules/auth/oauth2/controllers/oauth2.controller.ts:65 @Post("/token"), which carries client_secret, code, code_verifier and refresh_token - user-controlled and unauthenticated by construction, since obtaining a token is the point of the endpoint. Sink: this line logs requestBody = JSON.stringify(req.body) built at L18 plus headers = filterReqHeaders(headers) at L28, and the middleware is global - app.module.ts applies RequestIdMiddleware .forRoutes("*"). MITIGATION IS NONE, not merely weak: apps/api/v2/src/lib/filterReqHeaders.ts:6 explicitly re-emits Authorization: headers["Authorization"] ?? headers["authorization"], so the one filter on the path passes the credential through rather than dropping it, and mitigation-inventory.txt lists no redaction or masking wrapper for this file. Egress: apps/api/v2/src/main.ts:113 replaces the Nest logger with WinstonModule.createLogger(loggerConfig()) process-wide, and apps/api/v2/src/lib/logger.ts pushes Console unconditionally at L28 and the Axiom transport at L30 whenever AXIOM_TOKEN and AXIOM_DATASET are both set - so the write is unconditional and only the third-party egress is deployment-dependent.

description: Feishu twin of the same unauthenticated webhook compares attacker-supplied req.body.token to the stored token with ===, then persists the attacker's app_ticket into the shared credential record.
demotionReason: Broken-mitigation row on a medium-severity sink, so the truth table yields an advisory rather than a gate-block. The bypass is stated for the reviewer: the comparison at packages/app-store/feishucalendar/api/events.ts:66 is non-constant-time, the truth table's named weak mechanism, and the route carries no auth middleware - mitigation-inventory.txt lists only schema-validation lines for this file. Impact is bounded because the matched branch overwrites only app_ticket in the feishu-calendar app keys at packages/app-store/feishucalendar/api/events.ts:73-81; that value is a rotating ticket the app exchanges together with app_id and app_secret for an app_access_token, so a poisoned value breaks that exchange rather than disclosing either stored credential. Reaching the branch first requires recovering the token through a remotely observable timing difference in a V8 string comparison, which was not demonstrated. Reachability is narrower still: no in-tree writer provisions the Feishu key - scripts/seed-app-store.ts:136-145 carries a lark-calendar entry only, and the admin form schema at packages/app-store/feishucalendar/zod.ts:8 declares only the misspelled open_verfication_token - so reaching the comparison requires a system-wide admin write outside the form schema, which also fails rule-1 criterion (4). The pre-token im.message.receive_v1 and p2p_chat_create branches at :87 and :106 are reported as Layer 1 category 6 findings.

description: Unauthenticated Lark webhook decides trust by comparing attacker-supplied req.body.token to the stored token with ===; the sibling branch then writes an attacker app_ticket into the shared app keys.
demotionReason: Broken-mitigation row on a medium-severity sink, so the truth table yields an advisory rather than a gate-block. The bypass is stated for the reviewer: the comparison at packages/app-store/larkcalendar/api/events.ts:59 is non-constant-time, the truth table's named weak mechanism, and the route carries no auth middleware - mitigation-inventory.txt lists only schema-validation lines for this file. No empty-token shortcut exists: larkKeysSchema at packages/app-store/larkcalendar/api/events.ts:15 requires the key, so an absent value throws before the comparison, and the admin form writes the misspelled open_verfication_token declared at packages/app-store/larkcalendar/zod.ts:8, which is not the key this route reads, so no path was found that stores an empty open_verification_token. Impact is bounded to overwriting app_ticket in the lark-calendar app keys through prisma.app.update at packages/app-store/larkcalendar/api/events.ts:73-81, which breaks the app_access_token exchange rather than disclosing app_id or app_secret. Reachability is nonetheless in-tree: scripts/seed-app-store.ts:136-145 writes the correctly spelled open_verification_token for lark-calendar whenever LARK_OPEN_APP_ID, LARK_OPEN_APP_SECRET and LARK_OPEN_VERIFICATION_TOKEN are all set, and all three are documented for operators at .env.appStore.example:117-119, so a normally provisioned deployment does reach the comparison. The im.message.receive_v1 and p2p_chat_create branches at :87 and :106 run before any token comparison and are reported as Layer 1 category 6 findings under the check-16 routing rule.

description: The caller-supplied client secret header is compared to the stored OAuth client secret with !==, a non-constant-time check, and success returns the platform owner account, not a client-scoped one.
demotionReason: No demotion; this is the truth table's broken-mitigation row on a high-severity sink. Bypass: the comparison at apps/api/v2/src/modules/auth/strategies/api-auth/api-auth.strategy.ts:186 is non-constant-time, the named weak mechanism, and it is the only check between the caller-controlled secret header read at apps/api/v2/src/modules/auth/strategies/api-auth/api-auth.strategy.ts:60 and a successful authentication. mitigation-inventory.txt category 3 lists exactly five timing-safe call sites - apps/api/v2/src/vercel-webhook.guard.ts:46 and :53, packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:1 and :30, packages/app-store/btcpayserver/api/webhook.ts:85 - and none is in this file, so the repository owns the correct primitive and this path does not use it. Impact is platform-wide rather than client-scoped: on success L190-192 resolves the platform owner or admin through findPlatformOwnerUserId and findPlatformAdminUserId and L200 loads that user, so a recovered client secret yields that account's API access with no admin credential of the attacker's own.

description: The credential-sync webhook decides trust by comparing an attacker-supplied header to the shared secret with !==, a non-constant-time check, before writing decrypted app keys for any submitted userId.
demotionReason: The mitigation is the named weak mechanism but severity is medium, so the broken-mitigation medium/low row demotes it. Bypass: the comparison at apps/web/app/api/webhook/app-credential/route.ts:26 is non-constant-time and mitigation-inventory.txt category 3 lists no timing-safe call site in this file. What bounds it: the route returns 403 at apps/web/app/api/webhook/app-credential/route.ts:21-23 unless APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is set, so the endpoint is inert on a default deployment; the body must satisfy appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema declared at L12-18 and applied by safeParse at L32; and the keys are decrypted at L64-66 with CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY, a different key from the compared secret, so a recovered header alone does not yield storable credentials. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: Inbound calendar-subscription pushes are trusted by comparing the caller's channel-token header to the configured token with !==, so the sole trust decision on the sync route is timing-observable.
demotionReason: The mitigation is the named weak mechanism but severity is medium, so the broken-mitigation medium/low row demotes it. Bypass: the comparison at packages/features/calendar-subscription/adapters/GoogleCalendarSubscription.adapter.ts:41 is non-constant-time and mitigation-inventory.txt category 3 lists no timing-safe call site in this file. What bounds it: the unconfigured branch at L37-39 fails closed by returning false, so an unset GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_TOKEN denies every push instead of accepting it - the opposite of the fail-open pattern reported for packages/lib/rateLimit.ts:41; the token is a per-subscription channel value rather than a global credential; and a forged push only triggers a re-sync whose event data is re-fetched from the provider instead of taken from the request body. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: The cancellation-sync push handler validates the caller's channel-token header with !==, a non-constant-time comparison, so the trust decision guarding booking cancellation sync is timing-observable.
demotionReason: The mitigation is the named weak mechanism but severity is medium, so the broken-mitigation medium/low row demotes it. Reported separately from the subscription adapter because this is a distinct handler reached through a distinct route. Bypass: the comparison at packages/features/calendars/lib/cancellation-sync/handlers/GoogleCancellationHandler.ts:122 is non-constant-time and mitigation-inventory.txt category 3 lists no timing-safe call site in this file. What bounds it: L112-115 fails closed when GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_TOKEN is unset and L117-120 rejects a missing header, both returning false; and the handler resolves cancellation state from the provider rather than from request content. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: randomString draws every character from Math.random, a non-cryptographic PRNG, so identifiers built from it are predictable from observed output; it is consumed for OAuth username slugs.
demotionReason: Demoted because no user-controlled source reaches this sink and no secret depends on it, so rule-1 criterion (1) is unmet. The only production consumer is the username slug at packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:104, while every security-bearing value uses node:crypto - randomBytes(32) at packages/features/auth/lib/verifyEmail.ts:37 and :130, and crypto.randomBytes at packages/lib/crypto.ts:17 and packages/lib/crypto/keyring.ts:86. Severity low, therefore advisory.

description: The OAuth callback state query param is JSON.parsed and annotated as IntegrationOAuthCallbackState with no schema check, so any JSON type reaches consumers that treat returnTo as a string.
demotionReason: Mitigation exists and is functionally sound but scope-limited, so the functional-but-limited row applies. The constant-time nonce HMAC at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:26-32 discards any state a third party did not obtain for the victim's own session, so shape confusion is reachable only with the caller's own state - except for the five NONCE_EXEMPT_APPS declared at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:6 and short-circuited at L14-16, which return the unvalidated object. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: The unguarded calendar save callback JSON.parses the caller's state param and casts it to CalendarState with no schema check, so any JSON shape reaches its accessToken, origin and redir consumers.
demotionReason: No demotion; rule-1 is satisfied in full, which is why this is gate-blocking while the sibling type-confusion finding at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:12 is advisory - the criteria are identical and only the mitigation status differs. (1) the state query param is attacker-controlled; (2) the sink is production code; (3) NO mitigation validates the JSON branch - apps/api/v2/src/ee/calendars/controllers/calendars.controller.ts:275 casts with an as-assertion while the fallback branch at L278-287 validates the same four fields with calendarStateSchema.parse declared at L65-73, so the two branches disagree; (4) the route at L262 carries no UseGuards decorator, unlike every other route on this controller at L128, L140, L147, L199, L225, L309, L347 and L385. Verifiable consequence: a JSON state whose isDryRun is a non-string truthy value bypasses the schema branch's val === "true" coercion and reaches the dry-run early return inside apps/api/v2/src/ee/calendars/services/outlook.service.ts and gcal.service.ts before the getAccessTokenOwnerId check runs. Deliberately NOT claimed: the unconstrained redir target is a separate open-redirect concern present on BOTH branches because calendarStateSchema declares redir as an optional plain string, so it is not attributed to this defect, and the credential-saving path still requires an access token that resolves to a real owner. AGENTS.md forbids unchecked type assertions, so this is a standards breach as well.

description: The unauthenticated /save handler JSON.parses the attacker-supplied state query param under an unchecked OAuthCallbackState assertion, then uses its fields as a 301 redirect target and a bearer token.
demotionReason: No demotion; gate-blocking. Mitigation status is None. apps/api/v2/src/modules/stripe/controllers/stripe.controller.ts:80 declares @UseGuards() with no guard argument, so the route is unauthenticated even though mitigation-inventory.txt records that very line as an auth-middleware match - the clearest case in this run of a mitigation the deterministic layer can see but cannot evaluate. The state param is asserted rather than parsed at :101, and onErrorReturnTo is returned as the url at :116, :119 and :145 with no origin or relative-URL check, which @Redirect(undefined, 301) at :81 turns into a 301 Location. The same untrusted object supplies orgId and teamId into a server-side request path at :107 and accessToken into its Authorization header at :111. The organizations twin at apps/api/v2/src/modules/organizations/stripe/organizations-stripe.controller.ts:131 shares the assertion but sits behind six guards including ApiAuthGuard, so only this route is reachable unauthenticated.

description: Category 7 coverage, not a vulnerability: the unscoped booking.findMany here is service-authorized by the CRON_API_KEY gate at L19, and a global read is this cron's intended operation.
demotionReason: Not a vulnerability, so this record is counted as safe rather than as a finding: it is the category 7 coverage record for the 200 evaluated sinks, the mandatory severity field is set to the closed vocabulary's floor because no impact is asserted, and the cwe field names the category under assessment (CWE-862) rather than asserting an instance of it. The route is a system-wide cron whose service authorization is the CRON_API_KEY compare at apps/web/app/api/cron/bookingReminder/route.ts:19, so the PERMISSIONS.md resource.action model expects no user-level check on the unscoped read at :27. No tenant row reaches a caller: the handler returns only a notificationsSent count at :157 and the selected rows are consumed solely to mail the legitimate organiser at :144. Every one of the 200 evaluated category 7 sinks resolved to an authenticated, tenant-scoped or system-authorized path, so no missing-authorization instance exists to report. The weakness of that compare, and its acceptance of the secret in the ?apiKey= query string, is reported instead as the Layer 1 category 6 ten-endpoint family finding at apps/web/app/api/cron/webhookTriggers/route.ts:11, because line 19 is absent from sink-inventory.txt and the check-16 routing rule sends inventory-external findings to Layer 1.

description: Coverage: the routing-form page renders markdownToSafeHTML output through dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and sanitize-html's allowlist admits no script, style or on* attribute, so no bypass exists.
demotionReason: Coverage-only record; no vulnerability is claimed. sanitizeHtml runs over the rendered markdown at packages/lib/markdownToSafeHTML.ts:16 and its default allowlist admits neither script, style nor any on* attribute, and its default schemes exclude javascript:. The four rewrites at packages/lib/markdownToSafeHTML.ts:18-34 do run after it, but each only re-tags <ul>, <ol> or <a href= output the allowlist had already accepted and reorders <li>/<ul> nesting; none re-introduces caller-supplied text, and no bypass payload exists on this path. The template author is also the form owner, an authenticated tenant, so criterion (1) of rule 1 is unmet for a third party. Emitted per AAP 0.5.5 A9 so sink category 8 is covered without fabricating a finding. Severity low, gateBlocking false.

description: Category 9 coverage, not a vulnerability: no printf-style format sink is reachable here; the log.error argument is materialized into one string, so no specifier can consume attacker text.
demotionReason: Not a vulnerability, so this record is counted as safe rather than as a finding: it is the category 9 coverage record for all 38 inventoried sinks, the mandatory severity field is set to the closed vocabulary's floor because no impact is asserted, and the cwe field names the category under assessment (CWE-134) rather than asserting an instance of it. The template at apps/web/app/api/parseRequestData.ts:36 is fully materialised into a single string argument before log.error is invoked, so no trailing argument exists for a %s, %o or %j specifier to consume. The only inventoried multi-argument candidates interpolate an internal enum - packages/features/booking-audit/lib/service/BookingAuditTaskerProducerService.ts:109 and :136 - and the two performance.measure calls at apps/web/app/api/defaultResponderForAppDir.ts:76 and packages/lib/server/defaultResponder.ts:77 perform no printf formatting at all. All 38 evaluated sinks are therefore safe and no format-string instance exists to report.

description: Category 10 coverage, not a vulnerability: the method-keyed handler lookup cannot dispatch an injected property, because the guard at L11-15 returns 405 whenever the optional chain yields none.
demotionReason: Not a vulnerability, so this record is counted as safe rather than as a finding: it is the category 10 coverage record for all 15 inventoried sinks, the mandatory severity field is set to the closed vocabulary's floor because no impact is asserted, and the cwe field names the category under assessment (CWE-250) rather than asserting an instance of it. The truthiness guard at packages/lib/server/defaultHandler.ts:11-15 returns 405 whenever the lookup yields no handler, inherited members such as constructor or toString expose no .default property so the optional chain resolves to undefined rather than to a callable, and Node's HTTP parser restricts req.method to a known token set. The residual is the unchecked keyof assertion at :9 that AGENTS.md forbids, which is recorded here as a code-standard breach with no property-injection consequence; the remaining 14 inventoried bracket accesses index arrays or typed records with no callable target.

description: Coverage: all 19 inventoried filesystem writes are build, codegen or CLI scripts whose destination is a module-level constant, so no route reaches a write sink and no request value controls a path.
demotionReason: Coverage-only record; no vulnerability is claimed. The destination is built from __dirname at apps/api/v2/scripts/generate-secrets.ts:8, a compile-time constant with no request-derived component, and the module is invoked only by the generate-secrets script declared at apps/api/v2/package.json:37 - no route, controller or service imports it, so it is unreachable in a running deployment. The other 18 inventoried write rows are likewise codegen or tooling paths: apps/api/v2/src/swagger/generate-swagger.ts, apps/web/scripts/copy-app-store-static.js, packages/app-store-cli, packages/platform/*/scripts, packages/prisma/enum-generator.ts and scripts/. Emitted per AAP 0.5.5 A9 so sink category 11 is covered without fabricating a finding. Severity low, gateBlocking false. No secret value is recorded.

description: All six NextAuth cookies derive Secure and the __Secure- prefix from one useSecureCookies flag, and five also derive SameSite from it, so on an http deployment the session token loses Secure.
demotionReason: Mitigation is functionally sound but deployment-dependent, so the functional-but-limited row applies. httpOnly is set on the session token at packages/lib/default-cookies.ts:34 and the __Secure- prefix is applied at packages/lib/default-cookies.ts:18 whenever useSecureCookies is true, so a correctly configured HTTPS deployment is unaffected; the exposure requires a plaintext or misreported-scheme deployment. The nonce cookie is the one exception to the shared derivation: it hardcodes sameSite lax at packages/lib/default-cookies.ts:66 and takes only secure from the flag. SECURITY.md's out-of-scope list also excludes Secure and HttpOnly omission on non-sensitive cookies, which bounds the rationale without suppressing the finding. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: The payment id path parameter is fetched with no ownership predicate and the ownership test runs only afterwards, so the 401 versus 404 split becomes a cross-tenant oracle for which payment ids exist.
demotionReason: Mitigation exists and is functionally sound but scope-limited, so the functional-but-limited row applies. The membership test at apps/api/v1/pages/api/payments/[id].ts:56 blocks payload disclosure and withMiddleware("HTTP_GET") at apps/api/v1/pages/api/payments/[id].ts:70 enforces API-key authentication, so no other tenant's payment body is returned. It does not remove the existence oracle, because the 401 at L57 and the not-found catch at L62-67 are observably different, and the catch also serialises the raw error object into the response body. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: Category 14 coverage, not a vulnerability: no disclosure path exists; authorization precedes dispatch and schemaBookingReadPublic.parse at L119 narrows the over-fetched columns out of the response.
demotionReason: Not a vulnerability, so this record is counted as safe rather than as a finding: it is the category 14 coverage record for the 200 evaluated sinks, the mandatory severity field is set to the closed vocabulary's floor because no impact is asserted, and the cwe field names the category under assessment (CWE-200) rather than asserting an instance of it. Two boundaries cover this sink: authorization runs before dispatch, since apps/api/v1/pages/api/bookings/[id]/index.ts:12 invokes the middleware that throws 403 at apps/api/v1/pages/api/bookings/[id]/_auth-middleware.ts:92, and the payload is narrowed by schemaBookingReadPublic.parse at apps/api/v1/pages/api/bookings/[id]/_get.ts:119, which keeps only email, name, timeZone and locale of the related user. No successful-query path serialises the extra columns, so what remains is over-fetch and code-standard debt rather than exposure: the three @calcom/eslint/no-prisma-include-true suppressions at :105, :107 and :109 are dead after the migration to Biome, so the select-over-include standard in AGENTS.md now has no automated enforcement. That standards gap is reported without asserting a disclosure.

description: Authorising a single payment loads the caller's entire booking set with include bookings true, so every column of every booking is materialised purely to run an id membership test.
demotionReason: Demoted because the surplus rows belong to the caller and never leave the process: the query at apps/api/v1/pages/api/payments/[id].ts:47 is keyed on the session-derived userId at :48, withMiddleware("HTTP_GET") at :70 authenticates that caller, only booking ids are read from the result at :56, and the 200 response at :59 carries schemaPaymentPublic output alone, so userWithBookings is neither serialised into a response nor logged. What remains is excessive materialisation and unbounded cost: include: { bookings: true } at :50 pulls a whole collection whose size grows with the caller's booking history merely to test membership, and the @calcom/eslint/no-prisma-include-true suppression at :49 is dead after the migration to Biome, leaving the select-over-include standard in AGENTS.md unenforced. The raw error object serialised into the 404 body at :62-66 is a separate weakness reported as a Layer 1 category 9 finding. Severity low, therefore advisory.

description: Existing reminders are read at L83 and filtered at L95, the organiser email is sent at L144, and only then is the reminderMail row created, so concurrent runs both pass the check and send duplicates.
demotionReason: Mitigation is a broken mechanism but severity is medium, so the truth table's broken row yields an advisory rather than a gate-block. The only gate is the non-constant-time CRON_API_KEY compare at apps/web/app/api/cron/bookingReminder/route.ts:19, and no transaction, row lock or unique constraint spans the L83 read and the L146 write - contrast the SELECT FOR UPDATE lock the booking path takes at packages/features/bookings/lib/handleSeats/create/createNewSeat.ts:53. Impact is bounded to duplicate outbound reminder email with no data corruption, and SECURITY.md's out-of-scope list treats denial-of-service style amplification as out of bounty scope, which bounds severity without suppressing the finding.

description: The OAuth code query parameter is exchanged for tokens and the credential is persisted at L65 without checking which scopes Google actually granted, so a downscoped grant is stored as complete.
demotionReason: Mitigation exists and is functionally sound but scope-limited, so the functional-but-limited row applies. The route requires a session at apps/web/app/api/teams/googleworkspace/callback/route.ts:29, schema-validates the state at L40 and requires team-admin authority at L43 via throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam, so rule-1 criterion (4) fails - it is not exploitable without admin access to the team. The granted-scope check that packages/app-store/googlecalendar/api/callback.ts:55-57 performs against GOOGLE_CALENDAR_SCOPES is simply absent here. AUTHORITY CAVEAT for this finding: the OAuth2Client this route relies on is imported from googleapis-common, which is declared in NO workspace manifest while yarn.lock carries two independent transitive lines, "googleapis-common@npm:^5.0.2" at L24003 and "googleapis-common@npm:^7.0.0" at L24017. Which major supplies the client is therefore decided by hoisting, so this conclusion is version-indeterminate and must be revalidated once a direct version is declared. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: Category 17 coverage, not a vulnerability: the repository's only $executeRawUnsafe call is fully parameterized, and no eval, new Function or vm.runIn call site exists in this category.
demotionReason: Not a vulnerability, so this record is counted as safe rather than as a finding: it is the category 17 coverage record for the 200 evaluated sinks, the mandatory severity field is set to the closed vocabulary's floor because no impact is asserted, and the cwe field names the category under assessment (CWE-94) rather than asserting an instance of it. connectUsersToEventTypesQueryWithParams at packages/features/ee/managed-event-types/lib/handleChildrenEventTypes.ts:103-135 emits only positional placeholders at :124 and binds server-derived ids as parameters at :127-128, so no request value reaches the SQL text executed at :265. Sink-inventory category 17 also contains zero eval, new Function and vm.runIn call sites - every other hit is an identifier whose name ends in Function( or a setTimeout given a function reference - and a repository-wide search finds this the only Unsafe raw-query variant among the 305 inventoried raw-query lines.

description: The unauthenticated BTCPay webhook body is JSON.parsed here before any signature check, so an unsafe deserialiser on this path would be pre-auth reachable; the parse feeds a strict Zod schema inline.
demotionReason: Demoted because the category is clean at this sink and across its feed. JSON.parse instantiates only plain JSON values, so there is no gadget, prototype revival or constructor invocation to reach, and packages/app-store/btcpayserver/api/webhook.ts:54 constrains the result in the same expression with btcpayWebhookSchema.safeParse, returning 400 at :55 for anything off-schema; the signature is then verified in constant time by crypto.timingSafeEqual at :85-88 behind the length pre-check at :82, with a 400 at :89 on mismatch, so no unsigned payload can settle a payment. The feed carries no unsafe deserialiser either: of the 138 rows in Layer 3a sink category 18, 137 are JSON.parse and the single yaml.load, at apps/web/lib/apps/[slug]/getStaticProps.ts:35, is pinned to yaml.JSON_SCHEMA, which admits only JSON types and no custom tags, while sink-inventory.txt category 18 contains no deserialize( or fromJSON( call site at all. The ordering weakness that does exist here - the repository lookup at :62 and the credential read and parse at :68-73 running before verification, with observably distinct 404, 200 and 400 responses at :66, :67, :69, :73 and :77 - is a response-discrepancy concern rather than a deserialisation one, and is reported as a Layer 1 category 6 finding. Severity low, therefore advisory.

description: Coverage: 137 of 138 inventoried deserialization rows are JSON.parse, which instantiates no class, and the single yaml.load is pinned to yaml.JSON_SCHEMA over build-time repository frontmatter.
demotionReason: Coverage-only record; no vulnerability is claimed. The only non-JSON deserializer in the non-test tree is apps/web/lib/apps/[slug]/getStaticProps.ts:35, which passes schema: yaml.JSON_SCHEMA so js-yaml admits only null, bool, int, float, str, seq and map and no !!js tag, and its input is app-store markdown frontmatter read at build time rather than request data. The remaining 137 rows are JSON.parse, nine of them wrapped by a Zod safeParse, and JSON.parse can neither instantiate a class nor invoke code - prototype-named keys become plain own properties. No deserialize( or fromJSON( sink exists at all. The two pre-verification JSON.parse ordering weaknesses previously recorded here are not category-18 defects and are reported in findings-layer-1-arch.json category 6 instead, at apps/web/app/api/webhooks/retell-ai/route.ts:224 as CWE-696 and packages/app-store/btcpayserver/api/webhook.ts:62 as CWE-204. Emitted per AAP 0.5.5 A9 so sink category 18 is covered without fabricating a finding. Severity low, gateBlocking false.

description: Category 19 coverage, not a vulnerability: no XML parser is instantiated in the non-test tree; both DOMParser calls here parse as text/html, which resolves no entities and fetches no DTD.
demotionReason: Not a vulnerability, so this record is counted as safe rather than as a finding: it is the category 19 coverage record for both inventoried sinks, the mandatory severity field is set to the closed vocabulary's floor because no impact is asserted, and the cwe field names the category under assessment (CWE-611) rather than asserting an instance of it. The parser created at packages/ui/components/editor/plugins/ToolbarPlugin.tsx:371 is used with mimeType text/html at :373, and the second pair at :394 and :395 does the same, and the browser DOMParser never resolves external entities or fetches a DTD in HTML mode. Sink-inventory category 19 contains only these two lines, and no xml2js, libxmljs or SAXParser call site exists anywhere in the first-party non-test tree; node-ical 0.16.1 is present in the dependency set but its only import is the test-support package packages/testing/src/lib/bookingScenario/expects.ts:5. Both evaluated sinks are therefore safe.

description: getRawPayment puts the caller-supplied uid straight into payment.findFirst with no user, team or owner predicate, so any authenticated caller reads another tenant's payment row and clientSecret.
demotionReason: No demotion; this is the truth table's no-mitigation row on a critical sink. Source: the uid path segment of GET /v2/atoms/payment/:uid, bound by @Param("uid") at apps/api/v2/src/modules/atoms/controllers/atoms.event-types.controller.ts:142 and forwarded unchanged into getUserPaymentInfo at apps/api/v2/src/modules/atoms/services/event-types-atom.service.ts:399-400. Sink: this line's payment.findFirst({where:{uid}}), whose only filter is that uid. Mitigation: mitigation-inventory.txt contains ZERO rows for apps/api/v2/src/modules/atoms/atoms.repository.ts, so nothing is co-located; the only inventoried control anywhere on the path is the category-5 @UseGuards(ApiAuthGuard) row at atoms.event-types.controller.ts:141, which establishes that the caller is authenticated and never that the caller owns the payment - no membership, ownership or tenant predicate exists in either the controller, the service or the query. Reachable in production without admin rights: ApiAuthGuard admits any valid API key or platform access token. Impact is bounded by what the service returns at event-types-atom.service.ts:425-433 - the booking (with attendees), the payment row, the event type and clientSecret from getClientSecretFromPayment at :432. Payment uids are opaque but are handed to whoever books, so the value is not a secret between tenants. No secret or token value is recorded here. Corroborates the Layer 1 category 9 record at atoms.event-types.controller.ts:141.

description: getTeamEventTypes filters eventType.findMany only by the caller-supplied teamId, and its organization route runs with no authentication guard, so any anonymous caller enumerates a team's event types.
demotionReason: No demotion; this is the truth table's no-mitigation row on a critical sink. Source: the teamId path segment of GET /v2/organizations/:orgId/teams/:teamId/event-types, bound by @Param("teamId", ParseIntPipe) at apps/api/v2/src/modules/organizations/event-types/organizations-event-types.controller.ts:167. Sink: this line's eventType.findMany({where:{teamId}}). Mitigation: mitigation-inventory.txt contains ZERO rows for apps/api/v2/src/modules/teams/event-types/teams-event-types.repository.ts. The route's own inventoried category-5 row is @UseGuards(IsOrgGuard, IsTeamInOrg, IsAdminAPIEnabledGuard) at organizations-event-types.controller.ts:160 - those three guards validate that the org exists, that the team belongs to it and that the Admin API is enabled, and NONE of them authenticates the caller. Its six sibling routes on the same controller all carry ApiAuthGuard, at :80, :114, :137, :196, :223 and :254, and all but :137 also carry RolesGuard with @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN"); this route carries neither, which is why the omission is a defect rather than a design choice. Reachable in production without any credential. Impact: the include block at teams-event-types.repository.ts:120-133 returns users, schedule, hosts, destinationCalendar, calVideoSettings and the team's bannerUrl, name, logoUrl, slug, weekStart, brandColor, darkBrandColor and theme. Corroborates the Layer 1 category 9 record at organizations-event-types.controller.ts:160.

description: getVerifiedEmails passes the query-supplied teamId to getUserEmailsVerifiedForTeam with no check that the caller belongs to that team, so any authenticated caller harvests another team's emails.
demotionReason: No demotion; this is the truth table's no-mitigation row on a high sink. Source: the teamId query parameter of GET /v2/atoms/emails/verified-emails, coerced with Number(query.teamId) at apps/api/v2/src/modules/atoms/controllers/atoms.verification.controller.ts:121 and reaching this line unchecked. Sink: this line's getUserEmailsVerifiedForTeam(teamId), after which verification-atom.service.ts:86-93 pushes every returned member's primary email and each of that member's verified secondaryEmails into the response array. Mitigation: mitigation-inventory.txt contains ZERO rows for apps/api/v2/src/modules/atoms/services/verification-atom.service.ts; the only inventoried control on the path is the category-5 @UseGuards(ApiAuthGuard) row at atoms.verification.controller.ts:114, which proves the caller holds a credential and never that the caller is a member of teamId. The service's own teamId branch begins at verification-atom.service.ts:77 and performs no membership lookup before the query. Reachable in production without admin rights. Impact is a bulk email-address disclosure across tenants, usable for targeted phishing of a competitor's staff; no password, token or secret is returned and none is recorded here. Corroborates the Layer 1 category 9 record at atoms.verification.controller.ts:114.

description: getOAuthClientWebhooksPaginated selects whole webhook rows, so the list route that admits MembershipRole.MEMBER returns each webhook's signing secret and a member can forge signed subscriber payloads.
demotionReason: Not a demotion but the truth table's broken-mitigation row on a high sink: a mitigation exists and is bypassable by design because its role set is too wide. Source class: an authenticated MEMBER of the organization owning the OAuth client - the request needs only the clientId path segment. Sink: this line's webhook.findMany({where:{platformOAuthClientId}}), which uses no select or omit clause and therefore returns every Webhook column including secret. Mitigation actually present, all inventoried as category-5 rows in mitigation-inventory.txt: @UseGuards(ApiAuthGuard, OrganizationRolesGuard, OAuthClientGuard) at apps/api/v2/src/modules/oauth-clients/controllers/oauth-client-webhooks/oauth-client-webhooks.controller.ts:32, plus @UseGuards(IsOAuthClientWebhookGuard) at :74, :98 and :140. Why it is bypassable for this purpose: the two READ routes declare @MembershipRoles([MembershipRole.ADMIN, MembershipRole.OWNER, MembershipRole.MEMBER]) at :92 for @Get("/:webhookId") and at :109 for @Get("/"), whereas every mutating route on the same controller restricts to ADMIN and OWNER at :46, :69, :134 and :154 - so the guard chain runs and passes for a plain member on exactly the routes that return the credential. The response transformation does not strip it either: WebhookOutputPipe.transform destructures only eventTriggers and platformOAuthClientId at apps/api/v2/src/modules/webhooks/pipes/WebhookOutputPipe.ts:8, so secret survives in the rest spread at :9, and webhook.output.ts:43 declares readonly secret?: string with @Expose, which keeps it through plainToClass strategy excludeAll. Consumer proof that it reaches the client: apps/web/lib/hooks/settings/platform/oauth-clients/useOAuthClientWebhooks.ts:23 types secret?: string in its own response contract. Impact: holding the signing secret lets a member mint valid signatures for arbitrary payloads to the configured subscriberUrl. No secret value is recorded here - only its field name, declaration site and the roles that can read it. Corroborates the Layer 1 category 9 record at oauth-client-webhooks.controller.ts:92.

description: returnTo and onErrorReturnTo query params are copied into the OAuth state here and later become the 301 Location of the public callback, so an attacker-chosen absolute URL is redirected to unchecked.
demotionReason: No demotion; this is the truth table's no-mitigation row on a high sink. Source: the returnTo and onErrorReturnTo query parameters of GET /v2/conferencing/:app/oauth/auth-url, bound as bare optional strings at apps/api/v2/src/modules/conferencing/controllers/conferencing.controller.ts:101-102 with no @IsUrl, no origin allow-list and no relative-path constraint. Flow: both are copied verbatim into the OAuth state literal at :108-109, the state is JSON.stringify-ed into the provider auth URL by generateOAuthUrl at apps/api/v2/src/modules/conferencing/services/conferencing.service.ts:128-135 (:131 for Zoom, :134 for Office 365), the provider returns it to the callback, and the callback emits it as the redirect target at three separate points - :166, :169 and :180 - under @Redirect(undefined, 301) declared at :132. Mitigation: mitigation-inventory.txt lists seven category-5 rows for this file, at :69, :88, :131, :187, :202, :221 and :231; the auth-url route's own row is @UseGuards(ApiAuthGuard) at :88, which authenticates the caller and says nothing about the URL, and the row that guards the route that actually performs the redirect is the EMPTY @UseGuards() at :131. No redirect-validation mitigation exists anywhere on the path: mitigation category 2 (safeRedirect, isRelativeUrl, isSameOrigin, validateReturnUrl) has six rows repository-wide and none of them is in this file or in conferencing.service.ts. Reachable in production without admin rights: the caller needs only a valid access token to mint the state, and the victim-facing leg needs no credential at all because the callback is unguarded. The organization twin at apps/api/v2/src/modules/organizations/conferencing/organizations-conferencing.controller.ts:105-130 and :232-262 builds the same unvalidated state, but its callback at :233 does carry the full guard chain, so the exposure is specific to the non-organization route. No token value is recorded here.

description: The public callback casts JSON.parse(state) to OAuthCallbackState without validation, so attacker-shaped teamId, orgId and accessToken fields drive an internal proxy call and the redirect target.
demotionReason: Not a demotion but the truth table's broken-mitigation row on a high sink: a mitigation is present and enforces nothing. Source: the state query parameter of GET /v2/conferencing/:app/oauth/callback, bound as a bare string at apps/api/v2/src/modules/conferencing/controllers/conferencing.controller.ts:141 - the only check is a non-empty test at :146-148. Sink: this line's JSON.parse(state), whose result is type-asserted to OAuthCallbackState with no runtime schema, so every field is attacker-shaped. Consequences within the same method: :157 branches on decodedCallbackState.teamId and decodedCallbackState.orgId, :159 interpolates both directly into an internal URL, :162 sends decodedCallbackState.accessToken as an Authorization: Bearer header on that internal request, and :166, :169 and :180 use decodedCallbackState.onErrorReturnTo as the 301 target declared at :132. Mitigation that exists and why it is broken: mitigation-inventory.txt records a category-5 row for this route reading exactly @UseGuards() at :131 - an empty guard array, so the decorator is present and applies no guard, in contrast to the six sibling rows on the same file at :69, :88, :187, :202, :221 and :231 which all read @UseGuards(ApiAuthGuard). Mitigation category 9 (schema validation) has no row for this file, so no Zod or class-validator schema is applied to the state either. Reachable in production with no credential whatsoever. The organization twin at apps/api/v2/src/modules/organizations/conferencing/organizations-conferencing.controller.ts:249 performs the identical unvalidated JSON.parse, but its route at :232 carries ApiAuthGuard, IsOrgGuard, RolesGuard, IsTeamInOrg, PlatformPlanGuard and IsAdminAPIEnabledGuard - which is also why the unguarded route embeds a bearer token in the state at conferencing.controller.ts:111, namely to satisfy the guarded twin when it proxies to it at :165. No token value is recorded here.
